about: Homework for this pillar, one list per AI (Claude writes it; tools/kit/render.py in jpavia10/prometheus-hub turns it into docs/agents/QUEUE_{ai}.md and the Drive docs). Every task says exactly what to read, what to make, how many, where to save it, how Claude checks it and what makes it not done. A task is done only when the file passes the checks, never because it was sent.

tasks.title: Scan the house with a phone: 8 apps compared on 10 fixed columns
tasks.why: The house on the stand is placeholder boxes. The real model will come from Joseph scanning rooms with his phone.
inputs: each app's own site, App Store / Play listing and help pages
steps: Compare exactly these 8: Polycam, Scaniverse, Magicplan, RoomScan Pro, Canvas (Occipital), Matterport (phone capture), Metascan, KIRI Engine.

Columns, exactly: app | iPhone LiDAR needed (yes/no/optional) | Android | room floor plan with measurements (yes/no) | export formats (list) | GLB or USDZ export on the free plan | price per month (USD) | accuracy the maker states (with its words) | max area per scan | source URLs.
Every cell from the maker's own page, with the URL in the last column.

deliver.shape: one markdown table, 8 rows x 10 columns

tasks.done_when: 8 rows, 80 filled cells, every price and format on the cited page.
checks: Claude opens the source URL of every price and export cell for 4 apps at random.
rejected_if: a row copied from another row with the names changed
a source URL that does not open or does not say what the row claims
fewer items than the count
a file saved anywhere but the folder named here, or under another name
a blank cell without 'not stated' and the page you checked

tasks.title: The Hearth data shape: rooms with measured walls, the assets in each room, renovation projects (JSON Schema + 3 examples)
tasks.why: Rooms, assets and projects are empty on purpose. They need one shape before anything is saved. Hearth's scope (Joseph, 2026-11-05): renovation projects, the assets in every room, and a floor plan that gets accurate over time. Nothing else.
inputs: https://jpavia10.github.io/hephaestus-hearth/ (the desk today: the stand-in house, the room list, three project slots)
steps: Write one JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) with these records: house (name, floors, origin note); room (id, name, floor, outline = a list of corner points [x, y] in inches, clockwise, from one fixed origin per floor; ceiling height in inches; openings = doors and windows, each with the wall it sits on (index of the outline edge), offset from that wall's first corner, width, height, sill height); asset (id, name, category, room id, position {x, y, z} in inches + rotation in degrees, brand, model, serial, purchase date, price, receipt photo, warranty end, photos, condition, notes); project (id, room ids, title, state: idea / quoted / booked / doing / done, budget, start, finish, tasks, cost lines with vendor / quote / paid / date / receipt photo, before and after photos, asset ids added and asset ids removed); photo (file, room id, date, kind: room / asset / receipt / before / after).
Every length in inches (decimals allowed), every date YYYY-MM-DD, every id a short string; required fields marked.

Write 3 made-up examples in one JSON file that pass the schema: (1) a bedroom drawn with 4 corners, 1 door and 2 windows, holding 8 assets; (2) an L-shaped kitchen with 6 corners and a renovation that removes 2 assets and adds 3; (3) a bathroom remodel in state 'doing' with 4 cost lines.
Say the area of each example room in square feet (Claude recomputes it from the corners).
tasks.done_when: The schema is valid draft 2020-12, all 3 examples pass it, every stated area matches the corners, every asset sits inside its room's outline.
checks: Claude computes each room's area from its corners (shoelace) and compares within 0.5 sq ft.
Claude checks every asset position is inside its room's outline and every opening fits on its wall.
rejected_if: an example that fails its own schema
a room outline that crosses itself or is not closed
an opening wider than its wall
a real address, name, serial number or phone number

tasks.title: Home inventory: 120 asset categories, room by room, with the fields insurers ask for
tasks.why: Hearth lists what is in each room; the categories and the fields worth recording should come from a published home-inventory checklist, not guesses. Hearth's scope (Joseph, 2026-11-05): renovation projects, the assets in every room, and a floor plan that gets accurate over time. Nothing else.
steps: Use published home-inventory checklists: the Insurance Information Institute (iii.org), the NAIC (content.naic.org), FEMA / Ready.gov, or a major insurer's own checklist page.
List 120 asset categories across kitchen, bathrooms, bedrooms, living areas, office, laundry, garage, basement, outdoor and the house systems (water heater, furnace, AC, electrical panel, sump pump).
For each: category, the rooms it is usually in, the fields worth recording (from: brand, model, serial, purchase date, price, receipt, photo, warranty end, size), and the source page with a quote.
tasks.done_when: 120 categories, every one traced to a checklist page.
checks: Claude opens 10 source pages at random.
rejected_if: fewer rows than the count, or a row missing a field of the shape
a row copied from another row with the names changed
a URL that does not open, is a front page or a search page, or does not say what the row claims
a quote that is not on the page it cites (Claude opens 10 rows at random)
a file saved anywhere but the folder named here, or under another name
a category list from a blog instead of a checklist page

tasks.title: How accurate a phone floor plan really is: 12 published measurements
tasks.why: The layout must become accurate. Claude needs numbers on how close phone scans, phone AR and laser measures get to a tape measure. Hearth's scope (Joseph, 2026-11-05): renovation projects, the assets in every room, and a floor plan that gets accurate over time. Nothing else.
steps: Find 12 published tests (a paper with a DOI, a university or government test report, or a manufacturer's published validation) that measured floor-plan or room-dimension error.
Cover at least: iPhone LiDAR / RoomPlan, Android ARCore depth, a handheld laser distance meter, and a tape measure baseline.
For each: method and device, number of rooms or walls measured, the error as reported (mean and max, in cm or %), the room sizes, the DOI or URL and the quote with the numbers.
tasks.done_when: 12 tests, at least one per method named, every number quoted.
checks: Claude resolves every DOI and finds each quote.
rejected_if: fewer rows than the count, or a row missing a field of the shape
a row copied from another row with the names changed
a URL that does not open, is a front page or a search page, or does not say what the row claims
a quote that is not on the page it cites (Claude opens 10 rows at random)
a file saved anywhere but the folder named here, or under another name
an error number with no quote
a vendor marketing page as the only source for a scan method

tasks.title: 10 floor-plan and 3D formats Hearth could import: what each one carries

tasks.done_when: 10 formats, every cell traced to the spec or the three.js docs.
checks: Claude opens every spec page and checks each loader name on threejs.org/docs.

tasks.title: 10 home inventory and renovation apps taken apart: 50 features Hearth should have

steps: Apps: HomeZada, Centriq, Encircle, Sortly, Nest Egg, Under My Roof, magicplan, Houzz, BluePlan or Homer, and one more of your choice that tracks assets per room.

For each, 5 specific things on its screens about: assets per room, receipts and warranties, renovation projects with before/after, or the floor plan (example: 'tap a wall on the plan to see the paint colour and the date it was painted').
Each row: app, screen, what it does, a URL where it can be seen (help article, store listing, screenshot page), and how Hearth could do it better.
tasks.done_when: 50 rows, 5 per app, each about one of the three scope areas.
checks: A row about budgeting, shopping or maintenance reminders does not count (out of scope).
